meaning: assign a fixed meaning
note: Names a definiens; asserts nothing. The name class decides what may be defined (zp zq zr zh a claim; zm an act or method; zo an item; zv a value; zS a collection; zE a ✠ term only; zk an agent; zcr a criterion; zt only the atom t). Local to its message. A definiens that is quoted English is a scaffold (TF-5 Part C 0.5, D.2 item 11) and carries no SILEX meaning.

meaning: Mention the expression x. It is talked about, not used or asserted.
boundary: Quotation does not decide whether a bare expression is a command, a description or an assertion.
note: Mention: x is talked about, not used, asserted or evaluated. The result remembers the category of x (Mn[P], Mn[Q], Mn[Act], Mn[Ln]).

meaning: Time concept/value or variable; instant/duration/unit clarified by context.
note: Atom: "a time concept, value or variable". Its one fully specified use is as definiens of a time name, d≔(zt0,t). Other uses are not specified.

meaning: numeric zero
note: The number zero (not n0). Numerals other than 0 are unspecified outside ✠ (TF-5 D.3 item 1).

meaning: Logical truth-value constant in a specified interpretation or formal system
note: Logical truth constant "in a specified interpretation". No example. Not taught.

meaning: variable, unknown, or placeholder symbol
note: Placeholder symbol. A bound variable is written with a class prefix (zk zm zo zv zS), so bare x is not a bound variable.

meaning: Lexical unit; may be used as a typed atom in composition.
note: "Word": a lexical unit usable as a typed atom. No example. Not taught.

meaning: Novel relative to specified reference/context; default atomic adjective-like sense.
note: "New": novel relative to a reference; default atomic. No example.

meaning: Organizing elements into a collection; set union is only one kind of grouping.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,g∪(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 together as one group
r2_notes: A group you pass in adds its members. Three items: nest to the right.

meaning: Add or include a member within a specified set or structure.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,i+(zS1,zo1))  =  the group zS1 with zo1 added as one member
r2_notes: Adds a group as ONE member. Use g∪ to merge.

meaning: Remove an element from a set or from consideration.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,e−(zS1,zo1))  =  the group zS1 without zo1
r2_notes: Does not claim {2} was in it.

meaning: Analyze/decompose an item into relevant elements.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,a/(zo1,zcr1))  =  the parts of zo1 under zcr1
r2_notes: Does not say the list is complete.

meaning: Reduce the range of viable interpretations / uncertainty.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,c↓(zS1,zcr1))  =  the group zS1 narrowed by zcr1
r2_notes: May still have several members.

meaning: Seek an entity satisfying a condition; ∃ itself states existence, not a search process.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,s∃(zS1,zcr1))  =  the matches found in zS1 by zcr1
r2_notes: May be empty.

meaning: Mark or choose one item from a set of candidates.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,s⊙(zS1,zcr1))  =  one item chosen from zS1 by zcr1
r2_notes: Ties and best-ness not covered.

meaning: Identify an entity satisfying a specified condition, with a matching entity found.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(f∃(zS1,zcr1))  =  a search of zS1 by zcr1 found a match
r2_notes: n¬(f∃(…)) means "the search found nothing", not "it does not exist". This is a claim. To DO the search use s∃.

meaning: An agent/context's epistemically supported information representation or collection.
r2_examples: d≔(zS9,k▤(zk1))  =  what zk1 holds as supported knowledge
r2_notes: Members are not thereby true.

meaning: foundation / supporting premise set
r2_examples: d≔(zS2,b▁(g∪(⌜zp1⌝,⌜zp2⌝)))  =  zS2 is the premises group made of zp1 and zp2, neither asserted
r2_notes: Asserts none of them. Needs a group of ⌜quoted⌝ claims.

meaning: structured or processable content
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,d▤(zo1,zo2))  =  the data zo1 typed by the schema zo2
r2_notes: No truth claim.

meaning: Information content or a meaningful representation; mnemonic symbol, not established mathematical notation.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,i▤(zo1))  =  zo1 typed as an information item
r2_notes: No truth claim.

meaning: Turn an idea, problem or content into an explicit structured expression.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,f▦(zo1,zo2))  =  the source zo1 written in the format zo2
r2_notes: Fidelity not implied.

meaning: A defined function or input-output mapping.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,fƒ(zo1,zo2))  =  the function zo1 applied to zo2
r2_notes: Several arguments: put them in one group. Define functions with d≔.

meaning: Input or existing representation mapped to produced output; generation does not imply novelty.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,g↦(zo1,zm1))  =  something generated from zo1 by the method zm1
r2_notes: Not necessarily new or valid.

meaning: Map an expression to a meaning under an interpretation function.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,i↦(zo1,zcr1))  =  the meaning of zo1 under the framework zcr1

meaning: Change an existing object or representation.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,m↻(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 changed according to zo2
r2_notes: The original stays as it was.

meaning: Bring or acquire some specified object, value, or information into the current context
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,o←(zo1,zo2))  =  the item zo1 obtained from the source zo2
r2_notes: Does not say obtaining worked.

meaning: Process or mapping from a problem toward a solution.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,s↦(zo1,zm1))  =  a candidate solution to the problem zo1 by the method zm1
r2_notes: Success not implied.

meaning: Change a state or record using new information.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,u↻(zo1,zo2))  =  the record zo1 updated with zo2
r2_notes: A new item. The old one stays.

meaning: Assess an object against specified criteria, yielding a judgment or value.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,e⚖(zo1,zcr1))  =  the evaluation of zo1 against zcr1
r2_notes: Not validated truth.

meaning: A copy of the object x.
boundary: No automatic guarantee that the copy stays equal to the original, or that the original is preserved.
note: A copy of x. Result has the category of x. The copy is a distinct item; equality with the original needs s= and a criterion.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: d≔(zo2,⧉(zo1))  =  zo2 is a copy of zo1
r2_notes: A copy is a separate item. Holding the copy is not holding the original, and the copy need not stay equal.

meaning: A structured procedure with steps and possibly conditions.
r2_examples: d≔(zm9,m▦(zp1,zm1))  =  a method for reaching the goal zp1 by the acts zm1
r2_notes: A definition, not a run. i!(m▦(…)) defines it; to run it use its name.

meaning: An organized progression of operations or states
r2_examples: d≔(zm9,p▷(zm1))  =  a process made of the acts zm1
r2_notes: Not a running process.

meaning: A unit of work, potentially with objective, requirements, and completion criteria
r2_examples: d≔(zm9,t▦(zm1,zp1))  =  a task: do zm1, finished when zp1
r2_notes: Not an assignment.

note: Mathematical expression term. A term only: it never stands alone and is not wrapped directly in g← h◇ p◇ u? n¬. Closed list of places: object of cƒ, argument of r→ (two), argument of m> (two), definiens of a zE name. Grammar S1 to S7 inside the brackets.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(r→(✠(×(7,6)),✠(42)))  =  the value of 7 × 6 equals 42
d≔(zE1,✠(×(7,6)))  =  zE1 names the term 7 × 6
r2_notes: The maths inside ✠( ) has its own rules (FREEZE-6 T.3.6) that this guide does not repeat. A ✠ term cannot stand alone or sit directly in g←, h◇, p◇, u? or n¬. Say something about it with r→ or m>, or name it with d≔(zE1,…).

meaning: Count of relevant items or occurrences.
boundary: Needs a well-defined counted unit and domain. Not `k#` (key). A count is not a measure (`m∥`).
note: Count of the items of s; the unit and domain must be fixed by context. A count is not a measure (m∥). Used as an argument of m> (two counts).

meaning: sum suggests numerical calculation or aggregation.
note: Calculate/aggregate over a group. Overlaps cƒ (compute) and Σ inside ✠.
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,c∑(zS1,zm1))  =  the group zS1 combined by the method zm1
r2_notes: Math goes to cƒ(✠(…)), not here.

meaning: difference between entities / values
r2_examples: d≔(zo9,dΔ(zo1,zo2,zcr1))  =  the difference from zo1 to zo2 along zcr1
r2_notes: Numbers come from math terms, not from this root.

meaning: Logical negation of a particular proposition.
note: Negates a proposition and only a proposition. Never a question. n¬(r□(P)) is the proposition "P is not required". Scope: the argument only.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(n¬(zp4))  =  zp4 does not hold
r2_notes: The only logical negation. n¬(t≺(P)) and t≺(n¬(P)) are different (see the time group).

meaning: Conjunction of propositions.
boundary: N-ary use occurs. Formal arity and operand typing are not settled. The comma separates arguments; it is never an automatic AND.
note: Conjunction. Operands share one category: all claims, or all acts. Never a mix. Three or more operands are read as right-nested binary conjunction (TF-5 CL-2 reference form). With the content reading of h◇ and p◇ (LF-4), status-content may be joined; force markers (g← u? …) never are.
r2_header: ∧(claim, claim)  or  ∧(act, act) → claim or act
r2_examples: g←(∧(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 and zp2 are both true
i!(∧(zm1,zm2))  =  do zm1 and zm2
r2_notes: Three or more: nest to the right, ∧(zp1,∧(zp2,zp3)). The same root joins two acts under i!.

meaning: Present or refer to alternatives.
note: Alternatives. Claims: inclusive reading, two or more. Declared candidate items: a list of candidates with no truth value. Mixed or undeclared operands: a?. "Exactly one of n" has no short form (OG-18).
r2_examples: g←(a|(zp1,zp2,zp3))  =  at least one of zp1, zp2, zp3 is true
r2_notes: Does not say only one.

meaning: Existence. `∃(v,φ)`: v is bound locally in φ ("some v satisfies φ"). Bare `∃(x)`: the referent of x exists in a stated domain.
boundary: A positive claim may rely on a recoverable domain. A **negated** existence claim needs an explicit domain. Binding details are unresolved. Not `f∃` (find) and not `s∃` (search).
note: ∃(v,φ): some v satisfies φ; v is bound inside φ only. ∃(x): the referent of x exists in a stated domain. Negated existence needs an explicit domain, written as a conjunct ∈(v,S) of φ. Binding of nested or repeated binders is OPEN.
r2_examples: g←(∃(zkx,∧(∈(zkx,zS1),c⊃(zt0,t≺(h⊡(zkx,zo1))))))  =  some member zkx of zS1 held zo1 at some time before r (zt0)
g←(∃(zo1))  =  zo1 exists in a stated domain (the one-slot form)
r2_notes: The variable is a name that starts zk, zm, zo, zv or zS. Write the domain inside the claim: ∧(∈(v,S),…). Negated existence always needs an explicit domain.

meaning: Implication relationship between propositions.
note: Proposition-level implication: antecedent first. Does not establish either side.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(i→(zp6,zp7))  =  zp6 implies zp7
g←(n¬(i→(h◇(zp3),zp3)))  =  saying zp3 as a hypothesis does not imply zp3
r2_notes: Antecedent first. Does not establish either side.

meaning: Conditional premise determining when a consequent applies.
note: Conditional premise: condition first. A directive consequent is established only for i!(…). Any other consequent type is OPEN (OG-10). Rule or material conditional: OPEN.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED; TF-5 OPEN: consequent type (OG-10)
r2_examples: g←(i⇒(zp1,zp2))  =  conditional premise: when zp1 holds, zp2 applies (zp1 is not asserted)
r□(i⇒(zp7,i!(▶(zm1))))  =  it is required: if zp7 holds, execute zm1
r2_notes: Condition first. What may follow it is OPEN (OG-10). A standing rule uses r□ outside.

meaning: Enclosing information framework within which content is interpreted.
note: x is considered within ctx. ctx is an assumption ~(P) or a declared time name. The second argument is a claim, never a question. Neither ctx nor x is asserted outside. Criterion as context (TF-6 D7) is a candidate.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(c⊃(~(zp13),zp14))  =  within the assumption zp13, zp14 is considered
d≔(zt0,t)
g←(c⊃(zt0,∃(zv1,∈(zv1,zS1))))  =  in the context of the time name zt0, some zv1 is in zS1
r2_notes: The second slot is a claim, never a question. Neither the context nor the claim is asserted outside the context.

meaning: A condition or logical if–then implication.
note: Part B: "a condition or logical if-then implication". No recorded arity. Overlaps i→ and i⇒. Not used; write a?.

meaning: Supply evidence or a reason in favor of a claim.
note: Support first, then the claim. Support is not proof.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(s∵(zp15,zp16))  =  zp15 is offered as support for zp16
g←(zkq:s∵(zp19,zp20))  =  zkq says: zp19 supports zp20
r2_notes: Support first, then the claim. Support is not proof.

meaning: Standalone reason-giving connective; grounds supplied or recoverable from context.
r2_examples: g←(∵(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 is offered as the ground of zp2
r2_notes: Ground first, claim second. Offered, not proof.

meaning: Basis or cause given for an inference/conclusion (∵, because).
r2_examples: g←(r∵(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 is the reason given for zp2

meaning: Supply reasons, evidence, or grounds for a claim, decision, or action.
r2_examples: g←(j∵(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 is offered as justification of zp2
r2_notes: For ethical or decision grounds.

meaning: Supply a reason, mechanism, or justification for a statement.
r2_examples: g←(e∵(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 explains zp2
r2_notes: The explanation may be poor.

meaning: Therefore: reach a conclusion from premises or evidence.
note: Conclude from premises or evidence. The proposal gives (premises, claim); E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(c∴(zS1,zp1))  =  zp1 was concluded from the premises zS1
r2_notes: Build premises with b▁ (see recipes). Not proof.

meaning: Conclusion/discourse marker linking an already established basis to a subsequent claim
note: TF-5 writes a prefix line "∴ P" (example C12) with no signature and an implicit backward scope. This draft does not carry a prefix form; see issue U-02.

meaning: obtain by rule-based inference
note: Derived item first, then what it was derived from. Does not establish the premises or the validity of the derivation.
r2_header: d⊢(derived item, what it came from) → claim
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(d⊢(zp8,∧(zp1,zp2)))  =  zp8 was derived from "zp1 and zp2"
r2_notes: Derived item first. Does not establish the parts or that the derivation is valid.

meaning: Derive a conclusion using premises and inference rules.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(i⊢(zS1,zp1,zcr1))  =  zp1 was inferred from zS1 by the rule system zcr1

meaning: Formal system of inference rules governing what can be derived from premises
r2_examples: g←(l⊢(zS1,zp1,zcr1))  =  zp1 can be derived from zS1 in the formal system zcr1
r2_notes: Says it can be derived, not that anyone did it.

meaning: Establish a conclusion under specified formal premises and inference rules
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(p⊢(zS1,zp1,zcr1))  =  zp1 is proved from zS1 under zcr1
r2_notes: Claims a complete proof. Nobody checks it here.

meaning: Information relevant to testing, supporting, or challenging a claim.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(e▤(zo1,zp1))  =  zo1 is relevant evidence for zp1
r2_notes: Evidence against: e▤(zo1,n¬(zp1)). Does not say it is enough.

meaning: Directed causal influence: one event contributes to producing another.
note: Cause first, then the effect. Does not say that either occurred (OPEN whether it entails occurrence).
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: h◇(c↝(zp17,zp18))  =  hypothesis: zp17 contributes to producing zp18
r2_notes: Cause first. Says nothing about either having occurred.

meaning: Restrict permitted possibilities or operations.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled; TF-5 OPEN: argument order of c⊣ (Part 1, "Two further points are OPEN")
r2_examples: g←(c⊣(zo1,zp1))  =  zo1 is subject to the restriction zp1
r2_notes: Describes a restriction; it does not impose one.

meaning: Boundary or restriction on a quantity, operation, resource, or possibility
r2_examples: g←(l⊣(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 must not exceed the bound zo2
r2_notes: v1 says upper bounds only; FREEZE-6 Part B says any boundary or restriction on a quantity, operation, resource or possibility. Unsettled.

meaning: Required relative to a specified rule, condition, or modal context, not merely preferable.
r2_examples: g←(n□(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 is needed for zp2
r2_notes: A dependency, not a likelihood.

meaning: Equality of entities or values with respect to a specified criterion.
note: Binary only. Same relative to a criterion that must be declared or inherited; with no recoverable criterion the expression is underspecified (a?). Ternary s=(x,y,κ) is not adopted. How a criterion attaches is OPEN (candidate: c⊃(zcr1,s=(x,y))).
r2_examples: g←(s=(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 are the same
r2_notes: The rule for "same" comes from context; if none can be recovered write a?(s=(…)) and do not invent one. Only two slots; never write a third. Not i≡.

meaning: Approximate equality / resemblance subject to a similarity criterion.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(s≈(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 are similar enough
r2_notes: Tolerance comes from context.

meaning: Identity or pattern match; identify a particular entity or pattern.
note: Identity or identification. Exact numeric identity is OPEN. Entity identity, value identity, pattern identification are different things.
r2_examples: g←(i≡(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 are the very same entity
r2_notes: Sameness by some rule is s=.

meaning: Match two entities or patterns under a specified criterion (not necessarily total identity).
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(m≡(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 match
r2_notes: The matching rule comes from context.

meaning: tell apart by criterion
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(d≢(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 are told apart
r2_notes: The rule for this comes from context.

meaning: Identify an observed entity or pattern as matching a known one (≡ is suggestive, not a requirement of strict equality).
r2_examples: g←(r≡(zo1,zo2,zcr1))  =  what is seen, zo1, is recognized as the known zo2 under zcr1
r2_notes: A judgment. Correctness not implied.

meaning: Compatibility across claims or states; symbol suggests equivalence, but is not the same as mere consistency.
r2_examples: g←(c≡(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 and zp2 can both hold at the same time
r2_notes: This is NOT "equal".

meaning: Incompatibility or disagreement between propositions or states.
r2_examples: g←(c≠(zp1,zp2))  =  zp1 and zp2 cannot both hold
r2_notes: For three or more: n¬(∧(…)).

meaning: positions do not match
r2_examples: g←(d≠(zk1,zk2,zp1))  =  zk1 and zk2 take opposite sides on zp1

meaning: preferable under a criterion
r2_examples: g←(b≻(zo1,zo2,zcr1))  =  zo1 is better than zo2 on zcr1
r2_notes: A description. A person's preference: b~(zk1,b≻(…)).

meaning: Standalone estimation / approximation; must distinguish relation from operation.
r2_examples: g←(≈(zo1,zo2,zo3))  =  zo2 is an estimate of zo1, based on zo3
r2_notes: Close-enough equality is s≈.

meaning: More of a specified quantity or measure than another.
note: More than. Two ✠ terms (atemporal, both defined) or two counts; a mixed pair is ill-formed.
r2_header: m>(thing, thing)  or  m>(math, math) → claim
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(m>(#(zS1),#(zS2)))  =  the count of zS1 exceeds the count of zS2
r2_notes: Two math terms or two things; never one of each (FREEZE-6 M7).

meaning: A precedence or ordering relationship among items/events
r2_examples: g←(o≺(zo1,zo2,zcr1))  =  zo1 comes strictly before zo2 on zcr1
r2_notes: Not a sequence of acts. Use s≺ for that.

meaning: A variable or entity's value under a binding or interpretation
r2_examples: g←(v=(zo1,zo2))  =  the name zo1 has the value zo2
r2_notes: Not d≔, which names without asserting.

meaning: Obtain a quantitative value for a property under a specified scale and unit.
r2_examples: g←(m∥(zo1,zo2,zv1,zo3))  =  object zo1, property zo2, value zv1, unit zo3: a measurement report
r2_notes: The value is a number-name (zv…).

meaning: Negative sign or polarity in a stated numeric, logical, or evaluative domain.
r2_examples: g←(n−(zo1,zcr1))  =  zo1 is bad on zcr1
r2_notes: Logical negation is n¬, not this. FREEZE-6 Part B also lets n− mean a negative sign or polarity in a numeric or evaluative domain, so its exact use is unsettled.

meaning: Satisfies applicable conditions, rules, or interpretation
note: x satisfies the applicable conditions or criterion. A claim of satisfaction; not an act.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(v⊨(zo1,zcr1))  =  zo1 satisfies the conditions of zcr1
u?(v⊨(zo2,zcr1))  =  it is not known whether zo2 does
r2_notes: Not the act of checking (that is v✓).

meaning: A proposition treated as established under specified evidence/context; ⊤ evokes truth.
note: Fact: a proposition treated as established under specified evidence or context. Factivity OPEN.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(f⊤(zp1,zcr1))  =  zp1 is treated as established under zcr1
r2_notes: Not unconditional truth.

meaning: Falsity under a specified interpretation; ⊥ evokes logical false.
r2_examples: g←(f⊥(zp1,zcr1))  =  zp1 is treated as false under zcr1
r2_notes: Mirror of f⊤.

meaning: An epistemic status indicating a proposition/value is established relative to agent, context, and standards.
note: Known: an epistemic status relative to an agent, a context and standards. TF-5: do not rely on an unprefixed k✓ (holder and factivity unsettled); prefer zkq:k✓(P). Factivity OPEN.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled; TF-5: holder and factivity not settled (C 5.4)
r2_examples: g←(k✓(zp1))  =  zp1 is established knowledge
r2_notes: Say who knows: zk1:k✓(zp1). Do not use it without a who.

meaning: Standalone correctness relative to agreed criterion; distinct from truth or yes.
r2_examples: g←(✓(zo1,zcr1))  =  zo1 is correct under zcr1

meaning: Standalone incorrectness relative to criterion; distinct from false/error.
r2_examples: g←(✗(zo1,zcr1))  =  zo1 is incorrect under zcr1

meaning: Mark an issue as solved/closed, under stated criteria (✓).
r2_examples: g←(r✓(zo1,zcr1))  =  the issue zo1 is marked resolved under zcr1

meaning: A candidate satisfying requirements of a problem; ✓ alone does not prove independent verification.
r2_examples: g←(s✓(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 is a solution to zo2
r2_notes: A candidate only, not verified.

meaning: Degree, interval, or range of uncertainty associated with an estimate or state.
note: Degree, interval or range of uncertainty attached to an estimate. E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(u±(zv1,zv2))  =  the estimate zv1 has the margin zv2
r2_notes: Both are number-names. The margin is the same both ways.

meaning: Probability or likelihood meets a contextually specified threshold
note: Likelihood meets a contextually specified threshold (the threshold must come from context). E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(l≥(zp1))  =  zp1 is likely
r2_notes: How likely comes from context. It is not a slot.

meaning: Quantitative measure of likelihood relative to model/context
note: Quantitative measure of likelihood relative to a model or context. E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(pℙ(zp1,zv1,zo1))  =  zp1 has probability zv1 in the model zo1
r2_notes: The probability is a number-name, never a digit.

meaning: Estimate an outcome not yet observed, from available information
r2_label: PROPOSED; TF-5: arity not declared (T.3.1 item 4)
r2_examples: g←(p⇢(zp1,zp2))  =  on the basis zp1, we predict zp2
r2_notes: Basis first. Not a promise of correctness.

meaning: Not supplied: the place or the role was not given. Not none, not zero, not unknown.
note: The placeholder of the grammar (Owner ruling, 1 Nov 07:29, replacing the word null). A bare atom, no arguments. It fits every place except the ones B-21 lists. It is not the number zero (the root 0) and not a claim about a data field.
r2_examples: g←(s=(n0,zo2))  =  the first place of s= was not supplied
r2_notes: Replaces the word null. The former two-argument claim "the field P has no value in Q" is withdrawn from this glyph.

meaning: Information origin, location, or pointer.
note: Derived item first, then its immediate information source.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(s@(zo1,zo2))  =  zo2 is the immediate source of zo1
r2_notes: Item first, then its immediate source. Not r@ (a reference).

meaning: y is reachable from x by **one or more** immediate-source `s@` edges (indirect or direct ancestry).
boundary: Cycles in the source graph can give `s@*(x,x)`. Irreflexivity holds only under an explicit acyclicity assumption. Completeness of the source graph is a separate assumption. Ancestry does not imply equal content or that the original is still stored.
note: Source is reachable from item by one or more s@ steps. Irreflexivity only under an explicit acyclicity assumption; completeness of the source graph is a separate assumption.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: ∴ s@*(zo1,zo3)  =  so: zo3 is a source of zo1, directly or further back
r2_notes: One or more s@ steps. If the source graph has a cycle, s@*(x,x) can hold. Having a source does not mean the original is still stored.

meaning: Point to a specified source, item, or location (@).
note: Pointer from x to y: not provenance (s@ is origin). With a message name as second argument it is the qualified reference "x as it stands in message zUk" (TF-6 D5 candidate) and has the category of x. The two uses are told apart by the category of the second argument.
r2_examples: g←(r@(zp2,zo1))  =  zp2 refers to zo1
r2_notes: Not where {1} came from; for origin use s@ (item first, then its source). FREEZE-6 also floats r@(x,m) = "x as declared in message m" as a CANDIDATE. Avoid that use.

meaning: The speaker asserts x from the speaker's stored knowledge. The speaker must be attributable.
boundary: Discloses claimed origin only. It does not mean x is true, verified, current or reliably remembered. It can survive forwarding as the content of an attributed earlier assertion.
note: The speaker asserts c from the speaker stored knowledge. Discloses origin only; not truth, verification or currency. Survives forwarding inside an attributed claim.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(zkp:⊛(zp1))  =  zkp asserts zp1 from stored knowledge
r2_notes: Only discloses claimed origin. Not true, verified or current. The speaker must be named.

meaning: Indicate a connection between entities (:).
note: Relation. Its colon collides with the attribution colon A:ψ (TF-5 Part C 2.6, OPEN): how to separate them in every position is undecided.
r2_examples: g←(r:(zo1,zo2,zo3))  =  zo1 and zo2 are related by the label zo3
r2_notes: Direction: from {1} to {2}.

note: Tense: c holds or occurs before / at / after the reference time r. r comes from the nearest enclosing c⊃(zt,…). A bare proposition is tense-unspecified, never present. Quantification is existential over times on that side of r; no interval bounds. Tense of a negation: see KD-1.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(c⊃(zt0,t≺(h⊡(zk1,zo1))))  =  relative to r (zt0): at some time before r, zk1 held zo1
r2_notes: n¬(t≺(P)) = at no time before r does P occur or hold. t≺(n¬(P)) = at some time before r P did not hold (only for states such as h⊡). They are not the same.

note: Tense: c holds or occurs before / at / after the reference time r. r comes from the nearest enclosing c⊃(zt,…). A bare proposition is tense-unspecified, never present. Quantification is existential over times on that side of r; no interval bounds. Tense of a negation: see KD-1.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(c⊃(zt0,t●(h⊡(zkI,zo1))))  =  relative to r (zt0): at r, zkI holds zo1

note: Tense: c holds or occurs before / at / after the reference time r. r comes from the nearest enclosing c⊃(zt,…). A bare proposition is tense-unspecified, never present. Quantification is existential over times on that side of r; no interval bounds. Tense of a negation: see KD-1.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(c⊃(zt0,n¬(t▷(o→(zo1,♙(zkI))))))  =  relative to r (zt0): at no time after r is zo1 output by zkI
r2_notes: n¬(t▷(P)) means only that P does not occur or hold at any time after r. It does not say refusal, intent or prediction.

meaning: Standalone next/successor indicator; no execution implied.
note: "Next / successor, no execution implied". E or P arity unsettled. Do not confuse with the tense marker t▷.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: g←(▷(zo1,zo2))  =  zo2 comes immediately after zo1
r2_notes: Nothing is executed.

meaning: initial point / start state
r2_examples: g←(b₀(zm1,zp1))  =  the starting state of the process zm1 is zp1
r2_notes: Not a start action.

meaning: still / so far / continuing / not completed at the present point
Ordered relation among elements.
note: Ordered sequence. Over acts (i!(s≺(ψ1,ψ2)): the acts in order) it gives an act; over claims it gives a claim; over items (r2 example g←(s≺(zo1,zo2)): zo1 comes before zo2 in a sequence) it gives a claim. Three or more operands nest to the right.
r2_header: s≺(claim, claim)  or  s≺(act, act) → claim or act
r2_examples: i!(s≺(zm1,s≺(zm2,zm3)))  =  do zm1, then zm2, then zm3
g←(s≺(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 comes before zo2 in a sequence
r2_notes: Three or more: nest to the right.

meaning: Condition of an entity or task at a specified time.
r2_examples: g←(s◷(zo1,zo2))  =  entity zo1 has the status zo2

meaning: A stage or next operation within a process.
r2_examples: g←(s▷(zm1,zo1,zm2))  =  the process zm1 at stage zo1 performs the operation zm2
r2_notes: Not performed.

meaning: Literal membership: x is an item of S.
boundary: Does not cover "present in encoded form" or "derivable from". Not `e∈` (example).
note: Literal membership: x is an item of s. Not "present in encoded form" or "derivable from". Used as the explicit-domain conjunct.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(∈(zo1,zS1))  =  zo1 is a member of zS1
r2_notes: Literal membership. Not e∈ (an example of).

meaning: An instance belonging to a class or illustrating a concept or rule.
r2_examples: g←(e∈(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 is an example of zo2
r2_notes: Not set membership.

meaning: One available candidate choice, or an explicitly specified set of candidates
r2_examples: g←(o|(zo1,zS1))  =  zo1 is one option in the group zS1
r2_notes: No choice made, no ranking.

meaning: A central representation for an idea or abstraction.
r2_examples: g←(c◉(zo1,zS1))  =  zo1 is a concept described by the attributes zS1

meaning: express properties / characteristics
r2_examples: g←(d⋮(zo1,zS1))  =  zS1 is the set of properties of zo1
r2_notes: Not complete, not checked.

meaning: An identifiable arrangement or regularity among properties/relations
r2_examples: g←(p▦(zo1,zS1))  =  zo1 describes a pattern shown by the instances zS1
r2_notes: Pattern not verified.

meaning: Arrangement of elements and their relationships.
r2_examples: g←(s▦(zo1,zS1))  =  zS1 is the group of parts that make up zo1
r2_notes: Relations among the parts: r:.

meaning: Functional whole composed of interacting components.
r2_examples: g←(s⊞(zo1,zS1,zo2))  =  the system zo1 with the parts zS1 has the intended function zo2
r2_notes: Intended, not shown.

meaning: A structured representation of a system, process, or relationship.
r2_examples: g←(m⊞(zo1,zo2))  =  zo2 is a model of zo1
r2_notes: Validity not implied.

meaning: A mapping from an expression to its semantic representation.
r2_examples: g←(m↦(zo1,zo2))  =  the expression zo1 means zo2
r2_notes: A fact about meaning, not the act of interpreting.

meaning: A scope-defined identifier or lookup key for an item, record, or value.
r2_examples: g←(k#(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 is a key for zo2
r2_notes: Uniqueness not implied.

meaning: Relationship between two entities or pieces of information; not necessarily symmetric
r2_examples: g←(l↔(zo1,zo2))  =  there is a directed link from zo1 to zo2
r2_notes: A labelled link is r:.

meaning: Standalone connection operator; directionality requires operands/type.
r2_examples: g←(↔(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 and zo2 are associated
r2_notes: No label, no direction, no cause.

meaning: Indicate overlap with the current objective or context (∩, not necessarily literal set intersection).
r2_examples: g←(r∩(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 is relevant to the objective zo2

meaning: Declare an entity's state or assigned value; English noun/verb scope requires later clarification.
r2_examples: g←(s≔(zo1,zo2,zo3))  =  entity zo1, attribute zo2, value zo3: a declared state
r2_notes: Not a change.

meaning: x is retained and accessible (retrievable).
boundary: Does **not** entail that x is unchanged, nor that x is recoverable from a different derived object. Whether it applies to entities or to information is unsettled.
note: x is retained and accessible. Not "unchanged", not "recoverable from a derived object". Entity or information: unsettled. A state predicate.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(⊡(zo1))  =  zo1 is retained and accessible
r2_notes: Does not say zo1 is unchanged. Whether it applies to things or to information is unsettled.

meaning: A task/question/requirement still requiring a resolution
r2_examples: g←(p?(zp1,zp2))  =  the wanted state zp1 differs from the current state zp2: a problem
r2_notes: Not solved by saying so. FREEZE-6 Part B reads p? more widely: a task, question or requirement still needing resolution. Unsettled.

meaning: Information flows into a process from a specified perspective.
r2_examples: g←(i←(zo1,zm1))  =  zo1 is an input to the process zm1
r2_notes: Not received, not processed.

note: Holder first, then the item. A state predicate. The holder must be an agent name (class zk) or a bound variable with prefix zk; another class is ill-formed. Does not mean understanding, reading, ownership, custody or permission to share.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(h⊡(zk1,zo1))  =  zk1 has zo1 in the relevant context
r2_notes: A state, not ownership, understanding or permission to share. The holder is a zk… name.

meaning: held but not necessarily verified stance
r2_examples: g←(b~(zk1,zp1))  =  zk1 believes zp1
r2_notes: Does not make {2} true.

meaning: Context-dependent reliance on a source, claim or process with defeasible confidence
r2_examples: g←(t~(zk1,zo1,zo2))  =  zk1 trusts zo1 for zo2
r2_notes: No confidence slot. Use pℙ or u± for that.

meaning: The target or purpose of an action/message.
r2_label: PROPOSED; TF-5: arity not declared (T.3.1 item 4: read as a?)
r2_examples: g←(i◎(zk1,zp1))  =  zk1 intends zp1 as the outcome
r2_notes: FREEZE-6 says the arity of intent is not declared. Use with care, or say a?.

meaning: A target or criterion that a task is intended to attain
r2_examples: g←(o◎(zm1,zp1))  =  the task zm1 has the goal state zp1
r2_notes: Reaching it is not implied.

meaning: Defined target / desired outcome of a task or process.
A task, agent, or goal requires particular information, a resource, or an action.
r2_examples: g←(n!(zk1,zo1))  =  zk1 needs zo1
r2_notes: Does not say {2} is missing.

meaning: Exclude / decline adoption of a candidate (−).
r2_examples: g←(r−(zk1,zo1))  =  zk1 rejects the candidate zo1
r2_notes: Reason: s∵. Not negation.

meaning: Directing progression or next operation with respect to a target.
r2_examples: g←(g▷(zk1,zp1,zm1))  =  zk1 is advised, to reach zp1, to do zm1
r2_notes: Advice, not an order.

meaning: Proceed in a sequence or follow a specified instruction.
r2_examples: g←(f▷(zk1,zm1))  =  zk1 followed the act specification zm1
r2_notes: Compliance, not the order of steps.

meaning: Add assistance, information, or capacity to a task. The + operator shares an additive/inclusion intuition with a+ (accept) and i+ (include), though their full meanings differ.
r2_examples: g←(h+(zk1,zk2,zm1))  =  zk1 helps zk2 with the task zm1
r2_notes: Not necessarily useful help.

meaning: Present a candidate, proposal, or possibility for consideration.
r2_examples: g←(s◇(zk1,zk2,zo1))  =  zk1 suggests zo1 to zk2
r2_notes: Not accepted, not done.

meaning: Information directed back about a previous output or action.
r2_examples: g←(f↩(zo1,zo2))  =  zo2 is feedback on zo1
r2_notes: Who gave it: zk1:f↩(…).

meaning: Acquire and register an observation concerning an object/event
r2_examples: g←(o▤(zk1,zo1,zo2,zo3))  =  the observer zk1 reports about zo1, aspect zo2, value zo3
r2_notes: A report, not a proof.

meaning: A message's intended interpretation has been recovered to the specified criterion.
r2_examples: g←(u✓(zk1,zo1,zo2))  =  zk1 reports that message zo1 meant zo2
r2_notes: Self-report, not measured.

meaning: Apply a computational function or process to obtain output.
note: Action root of the seven-marker construction (compute): first argument is the object, every later argument is a distinct role marker applied to one name. In a claim position the expression denotes the event-proposition "an action of that kind occurs with these arguments"; it is not asserted by being written. No marker says the action succeeded, arrived or was received.

meaning: A value or message emitted by a process
note: Action root of the seven-marker construction (output (emit toward a recipient)): first argument is the object, every later argument is a distinct role marker applied to one name. In a claim position the expression denotes the event-proposition "an action of that kind occurs with these arguments"; it is not asserted by being written. No marker says the action succeeded, arrived or was received.

meaning: Accept/commit an item into an accepted set or working basis.
note: Action root of the seven-marker construction (accept): first argument is the object, every later argument is a distinct role marker applied to one name. In a claim position the expression denotes the event-proposition "an action of that kind occurs with these arguments"; it is not asserted by being written. No marker says the action succeeded, arrived or was received.

METHOD: procedure or technique followed. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(cƒ(✠(×(7,6)),⌘(zm1)))  =  compute it by the method zm1

note: INSTRUMENT: tool or resource used. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(cƒ(✠(×(7,6)),⚙(zo1)))  =  compute it using the tool zo1

note: RECIPIENT: the entity the object is intended to reach. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(o→(zo1,↣(zkx)))  =  output zo1 to zkx
r2_notes: Who it is meant to reach. Does not say it arrived.

note: DESTINATION: endpoint toward which the object is directed. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(o→(zo1,☞(zo2)))  =  output zo1 toward the endpoint zo2

note: SOURCE: origin from which the object comes. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(o→(zo1,☼(zo3)))  =  output zo1 from the source zo3

note: BASIS: evidence or premise supporting the claim concerned. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(a+(zo1,⚓(zp1)))  =  accept zo1 on the basis zp1

note: AGENT: the agent that performs the action. A role marker takes exactly one name and is well-formed only after the first argument of cƒ, o→ or a+ (six D-LI01 glyphs reserved; ♙ added by TF-1). Each marker at most once per action; order does not change roles; an omitted role is unspecified, not absent.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(cƒ(✠(×(7,6)),♙(zkA)))  =  zkA computes 7 × 6
r2_notes: The performer only. Not attribution, not who reported or approved.

meaning: Investigate whether a statement meets a criterion or is correct.
r2_examples: i!(c?(zo1,zcr1))  =  check zo1 against zcr1
r2_notes: The outcome is not stated.

meaning: Compare values or objects on relevant dimensions.
r2_examples: i!(c≶(zo1,zo2,zcr1))  =  compare zo1 and zo2 on zcr1
r2_notes: State the outcome with b≻, s= or similar.

meaning: Investigate an open set of possibilities without a fixed outcome.
r2_examples: i!(e⋯(zo1,zm1))  =  explore zo1 using the method zm1
r2_notes: No finding is implied.

meaning: Pursue evidence to address an unresolved question.
r2_examples: i!(i?(?⊤(zp1),zm1))  =  investigate ?⊤(zp1) using the method zm1
r2_notes: No finding is implied.

meaning: Reason/consider/process a target under the current context, without asserting that a final result is available
r2_examples: i!(t⋯(zk1,zo1))  =  zk1 thinks about zo1
r2_notes: No conclusion implied.

meaning: Apply a resource, rule, tool, or method to a relevant target.
r2_examples: i!(u↦(zk1,zo1,zo2))  =  zk1 applies the resource zo1 to the target zo2
r2_notes: Result not implied.

meaning: Update a representation or behaviour based on information, evidence, or feedback
r2_examples: i!(l↻(zk1,zo1,zo2))  =  zk1 updates zo2 using the evidence zo1
r2_notes: Not general editing.

meaning: A positive change relative to a specified quality measure.
r2_examples: i!(i↑(zo1,zcr1))  =  improve zo1 on zcr1
r2_notes: Says nothing about the result.

meaning: Apply specified test cases or criteria to assess an object, claim or behavior
r2_examples: i!(t⚖(zo1,zS1,zcr1))  =  test zo1 on the cases zS1 with the pass rule zcr1
r2_notes: The outcome is not stated.

meaning: Submit a question/request for information.
note: Ask: submit a question or request for information. The act of asking, as opposed to the question line itself.
r2_examples: i!(a<(zk1,?⊤(zp1)))  =  ask zk1 the question ?⊤(zp1)

meaning: Directed demand for information, retrieval, or an answer
note: Query: a demand for information, retrieval or an answer. Retrieving an existing result is q<. E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled; TF-5 OPEN: operand type (OG-08, OG-09); TF-5 says only that q< retrieves an existing result
r2_examples: i!(q<(zk1,zo1))  =  ask zk1 to look up the result zo1 that already exists
r2_notes: Not for computing something new.

meaning: Standalone execution trigger; does not assert completion.
note: Execute: a trigger. Does not assert completion. Whether a top-level ▶(x) line has force is OG-13.
r2_examples: i!(▶(zm1))  =  start running zm1
r2_notes: Does NOT say it finished. Use c■ for that.

meaning: Bring an incomplete state to a completed state.
note: Complete. In directive position a completion act; in proposition position the completed state. A reported completion is not verified completion. A named act is lifted to a state only by c■(zm).
r2_examples: i!(c■(zm1))  =  finish the act zm1
g←(c■(zm1))  =  zm1 is done
r2_notes: In a claim slot it means "{1} is done". It is one of only six acts that may sit in a claim slot (c■ d↦ v✓ cƒ o→ a+). A report of completion is not checked.

meaning: Retry or repeat the operation x.
boundary: Not a revision (`l↻`, `m↻`, `r↻`, `u↻`). No general numerical retry-limit syntax exists.
note: Retry or repeat the operation. Not a revision. No retry-limit syntax.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: i!(⤿(zm1))  =  retry zm1
r2_notes: Not a revision. No retry limit can be written.

meaning: choose among options and settle a decision
note: Decide: choose among options and settle a decision. TF-5 shows only r<(zkq,d⊙(zo3)) (a request to decide zo3). E or P arity unsettled.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: i!(d⊙(zo1))  =  decide the matter zo1
r2_notes: List the options on separate o| lines. (v1 text for this row is cut off; the rest is a guess.)

meaning: map available information to a resolved value
note: Determine: map information to a resolved value (value first). As a claim: the value is determined by the information. Needs consistent information sufficient to fix exactly one value. Determination is not physical truth.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(d↦(zv3,zo5))  =  the value zv3 is determined by the information zo5
i!(d↦(zv3,zo5))  =  try to determine zv3 from zo5 (success not implied)
r2_notes: Value first, then the information that fixes it. One of the six acts that also work in a claim slot.

meaning: Check a claim or result against relevant evidence and specified criteria
note: Verify (item first, then the criterion). As an act: a request-able check. As a claim: x stands verified against the criterion. Requesting verification does not report success; an inconclusive test, a negative test and a process error are three different outcomes.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: r<(zkq,v✓(zp1,zcr1))  =  ask zkq to verify zp1 against zcr1
r2_notes: Asking for a check does not say it succeeded. FREEZE-6 puts v✓ in a claim slot only once (C14, inside i→). For "meets the criterion" use v⊨.

meaning: Confirm prior content against supporting evidence or criteria.
note: Confirm prior content against evidence or criteria. Act or result is OPEN (OG-08).
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled; TF-5 OPEN: act-or-result of c✓ (C 5.4; OG-08, OG-09); argument order not taught
r2_examples: i!(c✓(zo1,zp1))  =  try to confirm zp1 using the evidence zo1
r2_notes: Evidence first. An attempt, not a result. FREEZE-6 leaves open whether c✓ is an act or a result (OG-08).

meaning: Express an outcome of a process or inference (→).
note: Value claim: the value of a equals the value of b (atemporal; first the expression whose value is claimed). The only use of r→ with a recorded arity. Any other use (a result of a process or inference) has no recorded arity.
r2_examples: g←(r→(zE1,zE2))  =  the value of math term zE1 equals the value of math term zE2
r2_notes: Only for math terms (✠). See v1 M3.

meaning: A directive or action requirement.
note: Instruction: a directive or action requirement. Asks for an act; does not report it. Acts may be joined by ∧ or ordered by s≺ inside i!.
r2_examples: i!(zm1)  =  do the act zm1
r2_notes: Does not say it was done.

meaning: Seek information or an action from another participant (<).
note: Request: the party asked, then what is asked. With an act: asks the party to perform it and to report the outcome via r→. Read as "perform" or "inform" by the type of the operand (OG-09).
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: r<(zkq,▶(zm1))  =  ask zkq to execute zm1
r<(zkB,cƒ(✠(×(7,6))))  =  ask zkB to compute 7 × 6
r2_notes: Asks zkq to perform the act and report via r→. To look up a result that already exists use q<. If the operand's type is unclear, FREEZE-6 says write a?.

meaning: State a binding constraint or condition (□, without presupposing modal-logic necessity).
note: Requirement. Exactly one argument. A standalone top-level r□(P) has requirement force (TF-6 D6 candidate, replacing the TF-5 CL-1 reading). Immediate operand of n¬ gives the proposition "P is not required". Not under ∧, g← or c⊃.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: r□(zp11)  =  zp11 is required
g←(n¬(r□(zp11)))  =  zp11 is not required
r2_notes: Does not say the requirement is met. Stand it alone or put it directly under n¬. Never directly under ∧, g← or c⊃.

meaning: Ask for an identity, value, or missing attribute
note: Asks for the value, identity or object that the bound variable v takes in the body. v occurs in the body at least once, is local to the question, and is not declared by d≔ or bound by ∃. One variable per question; no nested ?=. Does not assert the body or that an answer exists.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: d≔(zt0,t)  =  declares the time name zt0 (it fixes the reference time r)
?=(zkx,∧(∈(zkx,zS1),c⊃(zt0,t≺(h⊡(zkx,zo1)))))  =  which member of zS1 held zo1 at some time before r (the time named by zt0)?
?=(zv1,m∥(zo1,zo2,zv1,zo3))  =  what value of zv1 makes this measurement report true?
r2_notes: The variable name starts zk, zm, zo, zv or zS and says what kind of answer is wanted. It must occur in the claim. Do not declare it with d≔. One variable per question.

meaning: Ask whether a proposition holds / its truth status
note: Asks whether c holds. Unary. The answer is exactly one of g←(c), g←(n¬(c)), u?(c).
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: ?⊤(zp1)  =  is zp1 true?
r2_notes: Answer with exactly one of g←(zp1), g←(n¬(zp1)), u?(zp1).

meaning: Ask for event time or temporal position
note: When: event time or temporal position. Unary signature not specified by TF-5 (T.6).
r2_label: PROPOSED; TF-5: listed as an ask-form; arity not recorded (read as a?)
r2_examples: ?◷(zp1)  =  when does zp1 hold?
r2_notes: Meaning guessed from ?⊤. FREEZE-6 lists a unary ?◷ as OPEN (no agreed signature). Confirm before relying on it.

meaning: Ask for the location or position of a referent
note: Where. Unary signature not specified by TF-5 (T.6).
r2_label: PROPOSED; TF-5: listed as an ask-form; arity not recorded (read as a?)
r2_examples: ?@(zp1)  =  where does zp1 hold?
r2_notes: Same note.

meaning: Request choice/identification of an item from alternatives
note: Which: choose from alternatives. The ternary form is OPEN; the explicit-domain form of ?= is the specified way.
r2_examples: ?⊙(zv1,zS1,zp1)  =  which zv1 in zS1 makes zp1 true?
r2_notes: FREEZE-6 calls the ternary ?⊙ OPEN. For "which member of S" write ?=(zkx,∧(∈(zkx,zS1),φ)) instead.

meaning: Request reasons, grounds or causes
note: Why. Unary signature not specified (T.6). Negating an interrogative act is OPEN.
r2_label: PROPOSED; TF-5: listed as an ask-form; arity not recorded (read as a?)
r2_examples: ?∵(zp1)  =  why zp1?
r2_notes: Same note as ?◷ (FREEZE-6: unary ?∵ is OPEN).

meaning: A standalone question marker (contextual interrogative) and proposed general-purpose interrogative modifier
note: Standalone question marker proposed as a general-purpose interrogative modifier. No recorded arity.

meaning: A negative response or refusal concerning an identified question, proposition, or request.
note: A negative answer to an identified question, proposition or request. TF-5 does not use it to answer ?⊤; there is no bare n⊘ line in an answer message.
r2_label: PROPOSED; E or P arity unsettled
r2_examples: n⊘(⌜?⊤(zp1)⌝)  =  a "no" to the quoted question ?⊤(zp1)
r2_notes: The question must be quoted. FREEZE-6 uses n⊘ only as a "no" to an identified question and never as the answer to ?⊤; answer ?⊤ with g←(…), g←(n¬(…)) or u?(…).

meaning: affirmative response or approval
note: Yes: affirmative response or approval to an identified question.
r2_examples: y✓(⌜?⊤(zp1)⌝)  =  a "yes" to the quoted question ?⊤(zp1)
r2_notes: Mirror of n⊘.

meaning: Provide a response to a question.
note: EXCLUDED by TF-5 (T.0 Excluded: undefined arity; not used in answers).

meaning: A datum, value, or premise supplied to the present reasoning context; not automatically verified.
note: Supplies c as information. Does not verify. Whether supplying asserts is outside the grammar.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: g←(zp1)  =  zp1 is supplied as content
r2_notes: Supplies, does not verify. If asked whether g← "asserts", FREEZE-6 says: not defined.

meaning: Mark a tentative, testable proposition or possible explanation. ◇ relates to possibility, as in s◇ (suggest), but does not by itself encode testability.
note: Presents c as a tentative hypothesis. Line reading: the act of presenting. Content reading: the proposition that c is presented as a hypothesis. Does not establish c.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: h◇(zp2)  =  zp2 is put forward as a tentative hypothesis
r2_notes: Does not establish zp2.

meaning: A proposition or outcome is admissible under a specified context or constraints
note: c is admissible under the context or constraints. Line and content readings as for h◇. Does not say c is true.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: p◇(zp2)  =  zp2 is admissible under the relevant context or constraints
r2_notes: Does not say zp2 is true.

meaning: A value, referent, or proposition is not known in the relevant context (distinct from a missing/null entry).
note: c is not known in the relevant context. Not negation. Content reading: new design suggestion (TF-6 embeds g← and u? only as the third operand of r>).
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: u?(zp3)  =  zp3 is not known
r2_notes: Does not say zp3 is false.

meaning: A proposition or assessment is not established at the required confidence/epistemic standard.
note: c is not established at the required confidence or epistemic standard.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: u~(zp14)  =  zp14 is not established at the required confidence
r2_notes: Neither this nor u? says the claim is false. If you are unsure which of u? and u~ you meant, say a?.

meaning: Confirm receipt or notice of a message, without agreement.
note: Acknowledges receipt of x (a mention, or a label). Receipt is not agreement.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: a.(⌜g←(zp21)⌝)  =  I received the line g←(zp21)
r2_notes: Receiving is not agreeing. The question form is a.(⌜?⊤(…)⌝) or a.(label).

meaning: Express agreement/alignment with a proposition.
note: Expresses agreement with c. Not verification. A declaration may be agreed (acceptance by restatement a=(d≔(…))).
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: a=(zp21)  =  I agree with zp21

meaning: Mark more than one possible interpretation or insufficient disambiguation.
note: Marks ambiguity or insufficient disambiguation of x. Not a question. The standing escape for anything OPEN.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: a?(zp10)  =  zp10 is ambiguous or underspecified
a?(s=(zv1,zv2))  =  no criterion for "same" can be recovered
r2_notes: Marks ambiguity. It does not ask whether the claim is true. Use it when you cannot tell an arity, a criterion or a meaning.

meaning: Put forward a candidate for consideration, without adopting it
note: Puts c forward as a proposal. Does not adopt it. Names introduced in a proposal remain proposals until accepted by restatement.
r2_label: TF-5 signature; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: p↗(h◇(zp9))  =  proposal: consider the hypothesis zp9
r2_notes: Put forward, not adopted.

meaning: A process, operation, or result contains an error relative to some criterion.
note: Marks x as containing an error relative to some criterion. Does not give the criterion or the correction, and does not say that a mentioned proposition is false. TF-6 D5 adds a message name as x.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: e✗(⌜g←(zp12)⌝)  =  the line g←(zp12) is marked as erroneous
r2_notes: Gives no criterion, does not say it is false, gives no replacement.

meaning: Change an earlier proposal/state after reconsideration (↻).
note: Marks x as revised or under revision. Does not give the replacement.
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: r↻(⌜g←(zp12)⌝)  =  the line g←(zp12) is revised or under revision
r2_notes: Does not give the replacement.

meaning: A proposition taken as a starting input for reasoning
note: Premise line: a proposition taken as a starting input for reasoning.
r2_examples: p▁(zp1)  =  treat zp1 as an assumption (v1 reading)
r2_notes: v1 reads this as "assume". FREEZE-6 Part B reads p▁ as "premise: a proposition taken as a starting input" and writes assumptions as ~(claim). Prefer ~.

meaning: Standalone assumption operator; temporary working premise; no truth guarantee.
note: Adopts c as a temporary working premise. Not asserted. A bare ~ does not govern later lines; use c⊃ to say what is considered under the assumption. A top-level ~(P) is a premise line. The second alternative records TF-5 Part C 3.7 / C19, which writes ~(zcr1) with a criterion name; a criterion is not a proposition, so that reading is kept only as an unresolved candidate (basis U). The criterion-context alternative of c⊃ (second alternative there) is the cleaner design (issue U-03).
r2_label: TF-5 root; sort typing by C: PROPOSED
r2_examples: ~(zp13)  =  adopt zp13 as a temporary working premise
g←(c⊃(~(zp13),zp14))  =  within the assumption zp13, zp14 is considered
r2_notes: Does not assert zp13. Putting ~ on a standard, c⊃(~(zcr1),…), is only a CANDIDATE.

meaning: A transferable information unit between AI participants.
note: Message. The proposal gives a three-argument claim; TF-6 D5 restricts m▤ to a two-argument header m▤(zU,zk). The two readings cannot both be kept without distinguishing by the category of the first argument (a message name versus an agent). See issue U-12.
r2_examples: g←(m▤(zk1,zk2,zo1))  =  zk1 sent zk2 the content zo1
r2_notes: A message exists. Not delivered.

meaning: Information directed inward to a recipient (←).
r2_examples: g←(r←(zk1,zk2,zo1))  =  zk1 sent and zk2 received the content zo1
r2_notes: It arrived. Not understood, not true.

meaning: Supply a response to an earlier message/request (>).
note: Respond. The proposal gives a binary claim; TF-6 D5 uses a three-argument answer line r>(zUk,⌜Q⌝,W) with W exactly g←(A) or u?(A).
r2_examples: g←(r>(zo1,zo2))  =  zo1 is the label of the message replied to and zo2 is the reply
r2_notes: Naming messages across turns is still open in v1.

meaning: The sender undertakes to perform the act a.
note: Undertaking line: the sender takes on the act a. A line, not a claim.
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r2 (tier P)
r2_examples: u⊕(▶(zm1))  =  I undertake to run zm1
r2_notes: Does not say the act is done, can be done or is binding.

meaning: The sender declines to perform the act a, optionally giving the claim why as its reason.
note: Declining line: the sender will not perform the act a. A line, not a claim.
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r2 (tier P)
r2_examples: d⊖(▶(zm1))  =  I decline to run zm1
r2_notes: Does not say cannot. The reason is a claim given as reason.

meaning: the time given by an ISO 8601 text (instant, date, week, time of day, duration, interval, repeat)
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: the time at which the event of the claim happens: when an act occurs, or the moment a state begins to hold
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: at or before the reference time, P
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: the criterion of being a v such that body
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: every member v of s satisfies body
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: x is a best member of s under crit
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: the number of members of s (at time at, when given), as a math term
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: the number the quantity q has for x (at time at), in the unit q names
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: the sum over the members of s of the number q has for each (at time at)
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)

meaning: relative to basis, the probability of the claim c is the number p, from 0 to 1
r2_label: ENTERED IN SPEC DRAFT r3 (tier P)
